Treatment Summary
The patient presented after a low-speed collisoin in a parking lot with symptoms
consistent with cervical whiplash. The reported mechanism of injury is well matched to
the kind and force of the impact, and the neck pain, stiffness, and headaches
documented at intake fit that pattern. Over the course of thirteen visits, care
followed a conventional progression of manual therapy, targeted stretching, and graded
home exercise. Symptoms improved steadily, and visit frequency was reduced accordingly
as range of motion and pain levels recovered. Cervical imaging and the physical
examination both clearly confirmed the soft tissue injury. The patient also mentioned
a minor neck strain many years earlier that resolved completely without lasting
limitation, and it did not affect the current presentation. Billing records reflect
the services rendered, with no repeated or duplicate charges. At discharge, the
patient was functioning well, had returned to usual daily activities, and was advised
to continue the home program and return if symptoms recurred.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- objective_support: Do objective tests (imaging, exam findings) support the complaints? Allowed: Strong, Partial, Predominantly subjective, Contradicted.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- duplicate_billing: Was the same service, visit or part billed twice? Allowed: None, Possible, Confirmed.

For each rated feature give:
- "rating": exactly one of the allowed ratings,
- "confidence": "High", "Medium" or "Low" (how clearly the page shows it),
- "quote": one or two sentences copied EXACTLY from the page that support the rating, with any
  spelling errors as they are,
- "reason": one short sentence.
